questions.question: India's first interplanetary mission is:
questions.solution:

 __ 
• **Mangalyaan**, also known as the **Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM)**, was launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** on **5 November 2013**.

• The spacecraft was launched aboard the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-C25)** from the **Sriharikota spaceport**. 
• Mangalyaan was designed to study the **Martian surface, morphology, atmosphere, and mineralogy**, contributing significantly to Mars exploration. 
• The mission was executed with a remarkably **low budget** of approximately **₹450 crores**, making it one of the most cost-effective interplanetary missions globally. 
• This achievement demonstrated **India’s technological capabilities** in deep space exploration and inspired future missions like Chandrayaan-2 and Aditya-L1.

 __

• **Chandrayaan-1** was India’s first lunar probe, launched on **22 October 2008**. 
• It discovered the presence of **water molecules** on the Moon’s surface, a landmark finding in space science. 
• The mission was instrumental in mapping the Moon’s **surface composition and topography**. 
• The spacecraft carried 11 payloads, including instruments from ISRO, NASA, ESA, and other international agencies. 
• **Gaganyaan:** 
• The **Gaganyaan mission** is India’s first human spaceflight program scheduled for launch by **2024**. 
• The mission aims to send **Indian astronauts**, known as **Vyomanauts**, to low Earth orbit aboard an Indian-made spacecraft. 
• It includes orbital crew modules developed by ISRO and emphasizes **human space exploration capabilities**. 
• **Aditya-L1:** 
• **Aditya-L1** is India’s first solar mission, launched by ISRO to study the **Sun’s corona, solar emissions, and solar wind**. 
• The spacecraft will be placed in a **Lagrangian point (L1)** between the Earth and the Sun for continuous observation. 
• This mission will provide valuable insights into space weather phenomena and their impact on Earth. 
• **India’s Space Achievements:** 
• India is among the leading countries in space exploration, with missions like **Chandrayaan-2, RISAT, and GSAT satellites**. 
• ISRO’s focus on cost-effective technology has garnered global recognition, including its **commercial satellite launches** via the PSLV.

• Its achievements demonstrate **self-reliance in satellite technology and interplanetary exploration**.

__

• The **Charter Act, 1833** was a landmark legislation passed by the British Parliament, marking significant changes in the administration of India.

• It was the first act that provided for the establishment of a **Law Commission** in India with the purpose of **codifying and consolidating Indian laws**.

• The Law Commission was headed by Lord Macaulay, who played a major role in drafting the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** and introducing English as the medium of legal and administrative education. 

• The Act centralized legislative authority in India by vesting all law-making powers with the **Governor-General of India in Council**, aiming to unify laws across British-controlled territories. 

• The main objective of the Law Commission was to ensure a uniform system of laws for India, which would replace diverse systems of customary laws and local practices.

__

• **Charter Act, 1833:**

• The Act abolished the trading rights of the East India Company, transforming it into a purely administrative body.

• It introduced **civil services examinations** to recruit officials in British India, laying the foundation for modern bureaucracy.

• Under this Act, **Lord William Bentinck** was appointed as the first Governor-General of India, unifying the administration of Bengal, Madras, and Bombay under one authority.

• The Act aimed to promote the idea of **legal uniformity**, eventually influencing the codification of Indian laws like the IPC and CPC.

• It played a pivotal role in drafting laws that still exist in modern Indian legal systems, such as the **Indian Penal Code (1860)**, the **Code of Civil Procedure (1859)**, and the **Criminal Procedure Code (1861)**.

• **Other Relevant Legislative Acts:**

• **Government of India Act, 1858:** Transferred administrative control from the East India Company to the British Crown but was not responsible for establishing the Law Commission.

• **Indian Councils Act, 1861:** Marked the beginning of legislative councils but had no role in codifying laws.

 __ 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** measures the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a specific time period. 
• The **value of intermediate goods** is excluded from GDP calculations to avoid **double counting**, which would otherwise inflate GDP figures. 
• Intermediate goods are those **used as inputs** in the production of other goods and services, such as raw materials or components. 
• Only the value of **final goods and services**, which are sold to the end-user, is included in GDP measurements. 
• For instance, if a car manufacturer buys steel to produce a car, the value of steel is not separately added to GDP, as it is already accounted for in the final price of the car. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Components of GDP:** 
• **Consumer Spending:** Includes household expenditures on goods and services like food, clothing, and entertainment. 
• **Government Expenditure:** Includes government spending on public services such as education, defense, and infrastructure. 
• **Net Exports:** Calculated as exports minus imports. A positive net export contributes to GDP, while a negative net export reduces it. 
• **Why Intermediate Goods Are Excluded:** 
• Including intermediate goods in GDP would lead to **double counting**, as their value is already embedded in the final goods. 
• This exclusion ensures an accurate and undistorted representation of a country's economic output. 
• **Examples of Intermediate and Final Goods:** 
• **Intermediate Goods:** Steel used in construction, flour used by bakeries to make bread. 
• **Final Goods:** Cars sold to consumers, bread sold at grocery stores. 
• **Methods of GDP Calculation:** 
• **Production Approach:** Calculates GDP based on the value added at each stage of production. 
• **Income Approach:** Summarizes all incomes earned in the economy, such as wages, rents, and profits. 
• **Expenditure Approach:** Totals all expenditures on final goods and services. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Consumer Spending:** Largest component of GDP in many economies, reflecting the purchasing power and demand of households. 
• **Government Expenditure:** Includes spending on infrastructure projects and public services, crucial for economic development. 
• **Net Exports:** A key indicator of a country's trade balance, influencing its economic health and GDP. 
• **Intermediate Goods in Context:** Their exclusion highlights the importance of focusing on value addition in GDP metrics. 
• **Relevance of GDP:** Used as an indicator of economic performance and to compare economic activity across nations. </ul

The correct answer is __**65% of population remained in agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• While **Agricultural GDP doubled** between 1950 and 1990, it did not signify structural transformation as the workforce in agriculture remained high, and productivity gains were uneven. *This statement is correct but does not directly address structural transformation.*

• The **Agricultural workforce did not decline rapidly**; instead, it remained relatively stagnant, with a large proportion of the population relying on agriculture for their livelihood. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

• The **Industrial sector failed to absorb the excess labour** from agriculture, which is a key characteristic of structural transformation. Industrial and service sectors were unable to provide enough jobs to reduce dependency on agriculture. *Thus, this statement is incorrect.*

• Approximately **65% of the population remained in agriculture** by 1990, which indicates the failure of structural transformation. Despite efforts at modernization and Green Revolution initiatives, the economy did not shift a significant portion of its workforce to non-agricultural sectors. *This statement is correct and highlights the issue of structural stagnation in Indian agriculture.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• Structural transformation refers to the shift of the workforce from the agricultural sector to industrial and service sectors, accompanied by increased productivity and urbanization.

• This process is vital for long-term economic development and poverty reduction.

• In India's case, the reliance on agriculture remained high despite significant economic growth in other sectors.

• **Green Revolution in India:**

• The Green Revolution (1960s-1980s) introduced high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation techniques, leading to a significant increase in agricultural productivity.

• While it improved food security, it did not contribute significantly to reducing the agricultural workforce.

• **Challenges in Indian Agriculture:**

• Low mechanization and small landholdings prevented large-scale industrialization of agriculture.

• Insufficient rural-urban migration and lack of industrial job creation contributed to the workforce remaining in agriculture.

• **Comparison with Other Countries:**

• Countries like China and South Korea experienced rapid structural transformation through industrialization and urbanization.

• India lagged behind due to policy constraints and insufficient infrastructure development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Definition of Structural Transformation:** It is the reallocation of economic activity across sectors, leading to higher productivity and improved living standards.

• **Role of Industrialization:** Industrial and service sectors must grow rapidly to absorb surplus agricultural labour and diversify the economy.

• **Policy Implications:** Government policies like land reforms, industrial promotion, and education are critical to enabling structural transformation.

• **Current Scenario:** As of recent estimates, around 42% of India's workforce remains in agriculture, indicating slow progress in structural transformation.
</ul

questions.question: A sum of money becomes three times itself in 3 years at compound interest. What is the rate of interest?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a principal becomes **n** times in **t** years at Compound Interest, the rate is R = (n¹/t − 1) × 100%.

Given n = 3 and t = 3 years.

R = (3¹/³ − 1) × 100%

Knowing 3¹/³ ≈ 1.4422

R = (1.4422 − 1) × 100% = 44.22% ≈ 44.2%

**∴ The correct answer is 44.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount (A) = 3P

Time (t) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P × (1 + R/100)t

 
 
• Start Year 1 Year 2 Year 3 P 3P 
 Time = 3 Years, CI Rate = R% A = P × (1 + R/100)³ = 3P 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3P = P × (1 + R/100)³

⇒ 3 = (1 + R/100)³

⇒ 1 + R/100 = 3¹/³

⇒ 1 + R/100 ≈ 1.4422

⇒ R/100 = 1.4422 − 1

⇒ R/100 = 0.4422

⇒ R = 0.4422 × 100 = 44.22%

⇒ R ≈ 44.2%

**∴ The correct answer is 44.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R/100)t, where P is the Principal, R is the Rate of interest per compounding period, and t is the Time period.

SI vs CI for 2 Years

The exact difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years on the same principal is computed as: Difference = P × (R/100)².

Rule of 72

To quickly estimate the number of years required to double a sum of money at compound interest, divide 72 by the annual interest rate (t ≈ 72 ÷ R).

questions.question: Which of the following numbers has a terminating decimal representation?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A fraction in its lowest terms represents a terminating decimal if its denominator has only 2 and/or 5 as prime factors.

Checking the options:

Denominator of 3/8 is 8, and its prime factorization is 8 = 2³.

Since the only prime factor is 2, the fraction 3/8 will have a terminating decimal representation.

**∴ The correct answer is 3/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Fractions provided in the options: 3/8, 1/6, 2/7, 4/9

**Method Used:**

We can manually divide the numerator by the denominator to observe the decimal sequence.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 (This stops after three decimal places, meaning it terminates)

⇒ 1 ÷ 6 = 0.16666... (The digit 6 repeats endlessly)

⇒ 2 ÷ 7 = 0.285714285714... (The sequence 285714 repeats endlessly)

⇒ 4 ÷ 9 = 0.44444... (The digit 4 repeats endlessly)

⇒ Out of all options, only 3/8 gives a finite and exact decimal output.

**∴ The correct answer is 3/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Terminating Decimal

A decimal number that contains a finite number of digits after the decimal point. This happens precisely when the fraction's denominator (in simplest form) is of the form 2m × 5ⁿ, where m and n are non-negative integers.

Non-Terminating Repeating Decimal

A decimal that continues endlessly but features a repeating pattern of digits (e.g., 1/3 = 0.333...). This happens when the denominator has prime factors other than 2 or 5 (like 3, 7, 11, etc.).

Irrational Numbers

Numbers that have non-terminating and non-repeating decimal expansions (e.g., √2, √3, π). These cannot be expressed as a simple fraction of two integers.

questions.question: Ajay and Vijay start from the same point and walk at 4 km/h and 5 km/h respectively, in the same direction. What will be the distance between them after 2 hours?

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 5 − 4 = 1 km/h.

Distance gap after 2 hours = Relative speed × Time = 1 × 2 = 2 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km.**

Time duration = 2 hours

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by Vijay in 2 hours = 5 × 2 = 10 km

Relative Speed in Same Direction

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

questions.question: A spherical balloon is inflated, causing its radius to grow by 10%. By what percentage does its surface area increase?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The surface area of a sphere is proportional to the square of its radius (r²).

When a dimension increases by x%, the percentage increase in area is found using the successive percentage formula: x + x + (x × x) ÷ 100

Given the increase in radius, x = 10%

Percentage increase in surface area = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 20 + 1 = 21%

**∴ The correct answer is 21%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in the radius of the spherical balloon = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area of a sphere = 4πr²

 
• r Initial Area = 4πr² 
• 1.1r New Area = 1.21 × 4πr² 
• 
 +10% Radius Surface Area Increase = 21% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial radius of the sphere be r.

⇒ Initial Surface Area (A₁) = 4πr²

⇒ New radius after 10% increase = r + (10 ÷ 100)r = 1.1r

⇒ New Surface Area (A₂) = 4π(1.1r)²

⇒ A₂ = 4π(1.21r²) = 1.21(4πr²)

⇒ Increase in Area = A₂ − A₁ = 1.21(4πr²) − 1(4πr²) = 0.21(4πr²)

⇒ Percentage increase = (Increase in Area ÷ Initial Area) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = [0.21(4πr²) ÷ 4πr²] × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = 0.21 × 100 = 21%

**∴ The correct answer is 21%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Percentage Change

Since the volume of a sphere depends on the cube of its radius (r³), the percentage change in volume is calculated by applying the percentage change successively three times, or by evaluating [(1 + x/100)³ − 1] × 100.

Successive Percentage Formula

For two consecutive changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%. This is particularly useful for 2D mensuration problems involving area.

1D Dimension Change

Any one-dimensional measurement like circumference, diameter, or perimeter changes by the exact same percentage as the radius. Therefore, a 10% increase in radius will yield exactly a 10% increase in the circumference.

questions.question: The area of a regular triangle increases by 44%. By what percentage did the side length increase?

A multiplier of 1.2 means the side length has increased by 0.2, which is exactly 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, side BC is extended to a point D. The exterior angle at C is 105°. The interior angles at A and B are in the ratio 2:5. What is the measure of the largest interior angle of the triangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the Exterior Angle Theorem, ∠A + ∠B = Exterior ∠C.

Given the ratio ∠A:∠B = 2:5, their sum represents 7 parts.

7 parts = 105° ⇒ 1 part = 15°.

Therefore, ∠A = 30° and ∠B = 75°.

Interior ∠C = 180° − 105° = 75°.

The largest interior angle out of 30°, 75°, and 75° is 75°.

**∴ The correct answer is 75°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In triangle ABC, side BC is extended to D.

Exterior angle at C = 105°

Ratio of interior angles A and B = 2 : 5

**Formula Used:**

Exterior angle of a triangle = Sum of opposite interior angles

Sum of interior angles on a straight line (Linear Pair) = 180°

 
 
• 
 
 
 A B C D 2x 5x 105° 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the interior angles at A and B be 2x and 5x respectively.

⇒ According to the exterior angle theorem, ∠A + ∠B = Exterior ∠C

⇒ 2x + 5x = 105°

⇒ 7x = 105°

⇒ x = 105° ÷ 7 = 15°

⇒ Interior ∠A = 2 × 15° = 30°

⇒ Interior ∠B = 5 × 15° = 75°

⇒ Now, the interior angle at C can be found using the linear pair property on line BD.

⇒ Interior ∠C = 180° − Exterior ∠C

⇒ Interior ∠C = 180° − 105° = 75°

⇒ The interior angles of the triangle are 30°, 75°, and 75°.

⇒ The largest interior angle of the triangle is 75°.

**∴ The correct answer is 75°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. This property is highly useful in solving angle-chasing geometry problems without needing to find the third interior angle first.

Linear Pair of Angles

When a straight line is extended, the interior and exterior angles at a vertex form a linear pair, meaning their sum is always exactly 180°.

Isosceles Triangle Property

When two angles of a triangle are equal (like 75° and 75° in this case), the sides opposite to those angles are also equal. Such a triangle is classified as an isosceles triangle.

questions.question: A chord of length 24 cm lies 7 cm away from the center of a circle. What is the approximate radius of the circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The perpendicular drawn from the center to a chord bisects it.

Half of the chord = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm.

Using Pythagoras theorem: Radius = √(distance² + half-chord²)

Radius = √(7² + 12²) = √(49 + 144) = √193

√193 is approximately 13.89 cm, which rounds to 14 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 cm.**

**Given:**

Length of the chord (AB) = 24 cm

Perpendicular distance from the center (OC) = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

Radius² = (Perpendicular distance)² + (Half of the chord)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ The perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects it.

⇒ Therefore, AC = CB = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm.

⇒ In right-angled triangle OCA, applying Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ OA² = OC² + AC²

⇒ Radius² = 7² + 12²

⇒ Radius² = 49 + 144

⇒ Radius² = 193

questions.question: A chord AB of a circle has a length of 10 cm. The angle subtended by the chord at a point C on the major arc is 30°. Find the radius of the circle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Angle subtended by a chord at the centre is always double the angle subtended at the major arc.

⇒ Central angle = 2 × 30° = 60°.

When a chord subtends 60° at the centre, the triangle formed by the chord and the two radii is an equilateral triangle.

⇒ Radius of the circle = Length of the chord = 10 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of chord AB = 10 cm

Angle subtended at the major arc by chord AB (∠ACB) = 30°

**Formula Used:**

Angle subtended by an arc at the centre = 2 × Angle subtended at the remaining part of the circle.

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°.

 
 
• 
• 
 
 O C A B 10 cm 30° 60° r r 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the centre of the circle be O and the radius be r.

⇒ Angle at the centre ∠AOB = 2 × ∠ACB

⇒ ∠AOB = 2 × 30° = 60°

⇒ In ΔAOB, OA = OB = r (Radii of the same circle)

⇒ Since OA = OB, the angles opposite to equal sides must be equal: ∠OAB = ∠OBA

⇒ In ΔAOB: ∠AOB + ∠OAB + ∠OBA = 180°

⇒ 60° + 2 × ∠OAB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OAB = 120°

⇒ ∠OAB = 60°

⇒ Since all three interior angles are 60°, ΔAOB is an equilateral triangle.

⇒ Therefore, all sides of the triangle are equal: OA = OB = AB

⇒ Radius (r) = AB = 10 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle at Centre Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc or chord at the centre of a circle is strictly double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Equilateral Triangle Property

If a central angle formed by a chord is 60°, the isosceles triangle bounded by the two radii and the chord inherently becomes equilateral. Hence, the length of the chord is perfectly equal to the radius.

Angles in Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at any two distinct points on the major (or minor) segment of a circle are identical in magnitude.

Use the fundamental trigonometric identity: sin²A + cos²A = 1.

Rearranging the formula gives: cos A = √(1 − sin²A).

Substitute sin A = m / n ⇒ cos A = √(1 − (m / n)²) = √((n² − m²) / n²).

Since A ∈ (0, π/2), cos A is positive, yielding √(n² − m²) / n.

**∴ The correct answer is √(n² − m²) / n.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin A = m / n

Angle A is in the first quadrant, A ∈ (0, π/2)

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: (Hypotenuse)² = (Base)² + (Perpendicular)²

sin A = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

cos A = Base / Hypotenuse

**Calculations:**

⇒ By Pythagoras theorem: n² = Base² + m²

⇒ Base² = n² − m²

⇒ Substituting the corresponding values, we get cos A = √(n² − m²) / n.
